name: Domain overview
description: How reads split between bacteria, viruses, fungi and other domains. Uses a superkingdom (domain, kingdom) column of a long profile table to summarise every sample at the top of the taxonomy, compares the domains between groups and lists the most prevalent taxa of the smaller domains, so a virome or mycobiome check needs no extra table.

inputs.label: Taxon profiles (long)
inputs.description: One row per taxon per sample with read counts and a column naming the taxon's superkingdom or domain. Group, subject and timepoint roles are carried into the per-sample table.

domain_column.title: Domain column
domain_column.description: The column naming each taxon's domain; auto picks superkingdom, domain or kingdom.

top_n.title: Taxa per domain
top_n.description: How many of the most prevalent taxa each domain lists.

rank.title: Taxonomic rank
rank.description: When the table maps a rank role, use taxa of this rank only.

min_reads.title: Minimum reads per sample
min_reads.description: Samples with fewer retained reads are dropped; 0 keeps every sample.

remove_artifacts.title: Remove curated artifacts
remove_artifacts.description: Drop taxa on curation lists with the artifact role first.

outputs.name: domain_per_sample
outputs.description: One row per sample: share of reads and number of taxa per domain, the dominant domain, plus group, subject and timepoint.

outputs.name: domain_by_group
outputs.description: Per group and domain: samples, samples with the domain, mean, median and maximum share.

outputs.name: top_taxa_per_domain
outputs.description: The most prevalent taxa of every domain with prevalence, mean and maximum relative abundance and curated role.

outputs.name: domain_shares
outputs.description: Share of reads per domain as box plots per group.

outputs.name: minor_domain_taxa
outputs.description: The most prevalent taxa of the domains other than the largest one, such as viruses and fungi.

citation: Built with pandas, NumPy and Plotly. Domains follow the superkingdom of the NCBI Taxonomy (Schoch et al. 2020). See README.md.
